source.title: Purrturbed but Stable: Human-Cat Invariant Representations Across CNNs, ViTs and Self-Supervised ViTs

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures human–cat input-domain alignment within individual frozen vision encoders. It does not measure whether representations of different models converge with scale, across modalities, seeds, mappings, or features, so its results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports alignment scores for human and cat views of paired scenes processed by the same encoder. These results are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"]: they are not comparisons between independently trained models. The paper also reports distribution-shift and paired-stability analyses, but those do not measure any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study compares each frozen encoder's representations of original frames with cat-filtered versions of the same frames. Every CKA or RSA score is computed inside a single model across two input domains. No score compares two independently trained models, two modalities, two seeds, or a mapping between models. The only contact with the claim is a cited remark that CKA is stable across architectures and runs (Kornblith et al.). The paper never addresses representational convergence between models, so cites_only fits better than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors also conclude that training objective, architectural hierarchy and capacity jointly shape cross-species invariance. They add that distribution-shift tests (MMD, Energy, Wasserstein) frequently reject even where geometric alignment is high, so geometry and distribution need complementary tools.
record.recipe_differences: No method for testing inter-model convergence from the original sources is applied; this study measures alignment between human and cat-view inputs within frozen vision encoders.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported alignment values differ across metrics (CKA-RBF, CKA-linear, and RSA) and across model families and layers. The paper reports peaks at different depths for supervised ViTs, CNNs, and DINO models; these are sensitivities in its human–cat input-domain analysis, not tests of inter-model convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-encoder alignment between original and cat-filtered frames varies by model family. Mean RBF-CKA is highest for DINO ViT-B/16 (0.8144), then ViT-L/16 (0.8057). The top CNN is EfficientNet-B3 (0.7017), and Swin models score about 0.46–0.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How invariant a frozen vision encoder is to a species-specific input transformation depends on its architecture and training objective.

fits_no_version.finding: For the same encoder, within-model human–cat alignment differs by metric. ViT-L/16 scores RBF-CKA 0.8057 but RSA 0.4647; DINO ViT-B/16 scores 0.8144 and 0.6980.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scores of representational invariance to input domain depend on the similarity metric chosen.

record.problems: The alignment aggregates have no uncertainty estimates stated alongside their values. The models are frozen pretrained encoders, and no capability or performance measure is reported. The cat-vision transformation is described by the authors as an engineering approximation rather than a complete physiological model. The paper reports significance testing and BH-FDR procedures for other analyses, but those do not establish inter-model convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No results for a listed claim version were omitted. The paper's additional mean cosine, mean L2, distribution-shift, paired-stability, and layer-specific results are not extracted here because they concern human–cat input-domain differences rather than any listed version's inter-model convergence behavior.

untested.parts: No alignment between independently trained models, and no trend of such alignment with scale or capability. Base vs large variants are compared only on within-model human–cat alignment.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between models.
No analysis of recurring features or circuits across models.
Metric dependence is shown only for within-model human–cat alignment (CKA-RBF vs linear vs RSA), not for convergence between models.
No test of incompleteness, plateau, or causes of alignment between models.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to none. Table 6's text layout is garbled: 'block0' appears only six times for seven models, and every model reports CKA-RBF max = 1.0000. That 1.0000 is likely a near-identity at the earliest block, which may inflate DINO means. Mean CKA-RBF values in r01–r35 match Table 3 where both tables report them.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of alignment between independently trained models as size or capability changes.
No vision–language model comparison or paired image–caption alignment.
No comparison across random initialization seeds or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired mapping test.
No recurring interpretable feature, neuron, SAE feature, or circuit analysis.
Although the study reports multiple metrics and input-domain results, it does not test metric/input dependence of convergence between models.
No test of whether inter-model alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
